title: Noor and the Mixtape
premise: Ulyana Eastwick, seventeen, has spent years holding her family together while her mother works hospital night shifts—cooking, tutoring, and keeping her siblings' secrets from teachers and neighbors alike. When a group chat called 'Noor and the Mixtape,' created by her late father for the four of them, starts receiving messages predicting events hours before they happen, Ulyana realizes the account was never deleted and something—or someone—is using it to reach them. As the predictions grow darker and point toward a fire at their apartment building, Ulyana must stop being the invisible caretaker and trust her siblings as equals. In the end, they prevent the tragedy not by hiding but by finally letting their neighbors, teachers, and each other see who they really are—and the mixtape's last message reveals their father recorded it knowing he wouldn't survive, leaving them his blessing to build lives of their own.
about_author: Lior Whitlock grew up in a crowded walk-up above a laundromat, where stories were the only inheritance that fit on one shelf. They write about loud families, quiet kids, and the strange magic hidden in ordinary group chats.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A chaotic morning: burnt toast, missing permission slips, little brother Milo's scraped knee, all managed before mom's night-shift car pulls away. Ulyana insists to herself she has it handled. Emotional beat: exhausted competence masking fear.

chapters.title: The Rules of Invisible
chapters.summary: Ulyana navigates school deliberately unnoticed while sister Zoya craves attention and Milo gets flagged by a concerned teacher. Flashback establishes how the family learned to stay off social services' radar after Dad died. Beat: the cost of invisibility.

chapters.title: Noor and the Mixtape
chapters.summary: Cleaning out an old phone drawer, Zoya finds dad's ancient MP3 player labeled 'Noor and the Mixtape.' The dead group chat with his username flickers alive. Beat: grief cracked open by wonder; family gathers around the screen.

chapters.title: First Message
chapters.summary: The chat posts: 'Zoya will dye a blue streak tomorrow.' Next day Zoya impulsively dyes exactly that. Ulyana dismisses it as coincidence, but Milo is thrilled. Beat: uneasy delight, first crack in Ulyana's rationalism.

chapters.title: Coincidence Math
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, methodical: she lists every prediction against probability like homework. Second prediction lands—a rainstorm canceling the bake sale. Beat: control fraying; denial becoming work.

chapters.title: The Third Prediction
chapters.summary: The chat predicts Mrs. Adeyemi will bring samosas to the stairwell. It happens, and the neighbor mentions dad used to trade recipes with her. Beat: the past reaching through the present; warmth laced with dread.

chapters.title: Who's Typing?
chapters.summary: Zoya's POV. She investigates the account: created by dad, dormant three years, now active from a device that shouldn't exist. She tells no one how scared she is. Beat: the rebel sibling discovering she can't hack her way out of mystery.

chapters.title: Milo Knows Things
chapters.summary: Milo quietly admits he's been talking to 'the phone ghost' for weeks—it asked him questions about the family. Ulyana's anger masks terror. Beat: guilt; the eldest realizing she missed what mattered most.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Prediction: 'Your mother will be home before dark.' Mom arrives early, shaken—the hospital had a near-miss predicted in a memo no one wrote. Beat: the supernatural leaks into the adult world; Ulyana almost tells her everything.

chapters.title: Almost Telling
chapters.summary: Family dinner scene where Ulyana rehearses confession and swallows it, protecting mom from one more impossible thing. The chat pings: 'She already knows.' Beat: the loneliness of protection.

chapters.title: The Mixtape Side A
chapters.summary: They play the actual tape: dad's voice between songs, jokes, a message 'for when you need me.' Each sibling hears something different in it. Beat: bittersweet communion; found family theme seeded via friends who join the listening.

chapters.title: Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: At school, Ulyana's careful anonymity collapses when she defends Milo publicly, earning both detention and unexpected friendship with classmate Dev. Beat: visibility stings and frees at once.

chapters.title: Prediction Seven
chapters.summary: 'The landlord will sell.' A realtor's sign appears on their building. Ulyana realizes predictions aren't just eerie—they're warnings they can act on. Beat: agency discovered inside fate.

chapters.title: Dev and the Doorbell
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. New friend Dev notices the Eastwicks' exhaustion and starts showing up with food and homework help, refusing thanks. Beat: found family expanding beyond blood.

chapters.title: The Chat Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: For five days, nothing. The family, oddly, misses it—they've started planning around its messages. Beat: dependence revealed; silence louder than prophecy.

chapters.title: It Says Our Address
chapters.summary: A single message: coordinates, then 'March 14th. Fire.' Their own building. Panic fractures the siblings differently—Zoya wants to investigate, Milo wants to hide, Ulyana wants to fix it alone. Beat: stakes made mortal.

chapters.title: Telling Mom
chapters.summary: Ulyana finally confesses everything. Mom doesn't laugh; she checks the smoke detectors, calls the fire marshal, and admits she saw dad's 'hunches' too. Beat: relief of shared weight; parent becomes ally.

chapters.title: Fire Marshal Reyes
chapters.summary: Reyes finds old wiring violations but needs proof of imminent danger to force repairs. The prediction gives a date, not evidence. Beat: bureaucracy versus intuition; frustration.

chapters.title: Zoya's Deep Dive
chapters.summary: Zoya traces the account's activity to a signal originating inside the building itself. Something in the walls? Or something left behind? Beat: mystery deepens toward the uncanny.

chapters.title: What Dad Built
chapters.summary: Following wiring diagrams, they find dad's old radio workshop in the basement—he'd rigged a mesh network and a message scheduler before he died. But the recent messages aren't scheduled ones. Beat: explanation arrives, yet mystery remains.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Listens
chapters.summary: Mrs. Adeyemi reveals dad used to predict things too—small hunches, always right. 'He said the house would talk after he was gone.' Beat: legacy reframed; magic rooted in love and attention.

chapters.title: Time Running Out
chapters.summary: Ten days to March 14th. Repairs stalled, mom working doubles, tempers flaring. Ulyana tries to do everything herself and fails spectacularly. Beat: the caretaker's breaking point.

chapters.title: The Fight
chapters.summary: Zoya accuses Ulyana of becoming a warden instead of a sister; Ulyana says the cruel true thing back. Milo overhears. Beat: lowest ebb; family fracture mirroring the building's cracks.

chapters.title: Milo Runs
chapters.summary: Milo disappears after school; the chat sends no warning—which terrifies them more than any prediction. Found at dad's grave, Milo explains he wanted to ask dad directly. Beat: grief given a child's face; reconciliation begins.

chapters.title: Asking Instead of Protecting
chapters.summary: Ulyana apologizes—not for caring, but for deciding alone. She asks each sibling what they actually want. Beat: leadership redefined as listening; labels come off within the family.

chapters.title: Plan of Small Loud People
chapters.summary: The siblings divide the mission: Zoya documents violations, Milo maps which neighbors are home when, Ulyana organizes. Dev and Mrs. Adeyemi enlist others. Beat: rising hope; ensemble energy.

chapters.title: The Petition
chapters.summary: They present tenants' complaints and Reyes's findings to the city. Partial win: emergency inspection ordered—for March 20th. Six days too late. Beat: victory soured; clock ticking louder.

chapters.title: One Last Message
chapters.summary: The chat breaks pattern with a personal note: 'You were never invisible to me. Look closer at 3B.' Beat: intimacy of the unknown sender; clue delivered like a gift.

chapters.title: Apartment 3B
chapters.summary: Empty unit 3B holds dad's backup server and a half-finished letter listing every 'hunch' he ever had—including one unfinished: 'On March 14th, tell them—' Beat: so close to answers; ache of incompleteness.

chapters.title: Finishing His Sentence
chapters.summary: Each sibling guesses what dad meant. Through arguing it out, they realize the message matters less than the fact that they're solving it together. Beat: thematic climax of belonging over certainty.

chapters.title: March 13th
chapters.summary: Eve of the fire. Evacuation plans rehearsed, neighbors warned, some disbelieving. Mom takes a rare day shift to be home. The chat goes silent again. Beat: held breath; quiet before catastrophe.

chapters.title: Smoke
chapters.summary: March 14th, 4:12 a.m.—smell of smoke before any alarm. The old wiring ignites behind the laundry room wall. Ulyana wakes the building door to door. Beat: adrenaline; every choice made visible.

chapters.title: The Stairwell
chapters.summary: Evacuation chaos: Mrs. Adeyemi's oxygen tank, a locked 2C door, Milo frozen on the landing. Siblings execute their plan imperfectly but together. Beat: courage as teamwork, not heroics.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: Building saved, one wing gutted—their apartment among the losses. Standing in the street in pajamas, they've lost things but kept each other. Beat: grief and gratitude entangled.

chapters.title: The Last Prediction
chapters.summary: In the ashes' aftermath, the chat sends its final message: 'Tell them I'm proud. Tell them to be seen.' Then the account closes forever. Beat: closure; the sender's identity left as grace, not puzzle.

chapters.title: Seen
chapters.summary: At the relief center, teachers, classmates, and neighbors surround the Eastwicks—the invisible family suddenly known, embraced, fed, helped. Ulyana lets them be helped. Beat: belonging achieved; vulnerability rewarded.

chapters.title: New Address
chapters.summary: The family moves into Mrs. Adeyemi's spare rooms and Dev's couch rotation—a patchwork household bigger than blood. Mom cuts back to day shifts because people showed up. Beat: found family fully realized.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Salvaging the melted MP3 player, they discover a second side of the tape they'd never played: dad's unfinished message, completed by his own recorded voice—advice for each sibling's future. Beat: tears and laughter; inheritance received.

chapters.title: Who Ulyana Is
chapters.summary: Ulyana applies to a journalism program across town, terrified and certain. Zoya claims the basement workshop; Milo joins the science fair openly. Beat: each sibling choosing a self beyond their role.

chapters.title: The Mixtape Plays On
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ulyana's POV: a year later, the rebuilt building hosts a block party; the mixtape plays from the rooftop. A new message appears—from Zoya, to future them. Beat: full-circle resolution; memory, love, and voice carried forward.
